# Actual global cap curvature and a one-fiber canonical escape

Flatness under a preliminary radial strictification is different from
flatness under moving the selected cap group. This note retains the
entire unchanged source's first and second cap derivatives. It gives an
exact quadratic criterion, and then evaluates that criterion for a
compatible family of centered homothetic simplices.

The resulting theorem changes only ONE fiber physically after
strictification. For any finite positive homothetic simplex family
with an affine centroid section, at least two fibers, and d >= 2, a
smallest-radius fiber admits an actual joint escape with a moving
common meeting point and fixed continuous cap normals. All selected
canonical cap budgets decrease and total mixed volume increases.
The other fibers contribute nonzero cap curvature throughout.
This concerns one selected covering group; it is not an OC conclusion.

## 1. A general baseline identity

Let P be the finite lattice-complete positive support of an actual
compatible full-dimensional d-fiber family, d >= 2. Suppose an affine
section q(z) is interior to every fiber. Shear q to zero. At a selected
base p let the fiber be a centered simplex K of volume V, with
barycentrics
\[
 \lambda_i(x)=l_i(x)+1/m,\qquad m=d+1,\quad
 h=d/m,\quad \Gamma=h^d.
\]
The initial selected group is H_i={l_i(x)>=0}. It covers the whole
ambient space because its margins sum to zero.

Let theta be ANY smooth finite-dimensional cap-parameter chart that
preserves this whole-space cover, with theta=0 the original tuple.
It may include threshold changes affine in z and changes of the
continuous normals. We require the actual cap functions below to be
C^2 near the initial configuration. Proper sections alone do not
guarantee C^2 regularity; a polytope plane passing through a vertex can
require a separate one-sided treatment.

Write K(W) for the physical labeled simplex whose barycentric vertex
matrix W has column sums one; W=I initially. Define
\[
 F_i(W,\theta)=|K(W)\cap H_i(\theta)_p|,\qquad
 G_i(\theta)=\sum_{z\in P}|K_z\cap H_i(\theta)_z|.
\]
The EXACT global cap increment is
\[
 c_i(W,\theta)
   =F_i(W,\theta)-F_i(I,\theta)+G_i(\theta)-G_i(0).       \tag{1}
\]
Thus the unchanged fibers have not been dropped. Total mixed mass
changes by V(det W-1).

For a physical velocity B, whose column sums are zero, put
T=tr B and r=B 1. The canonical cap derivative is
\[
 f_i(B)=D_WF_i(I,0)[B]=V\Gamma(T+r_i).                 \tag{2}
\]
It is onto R^m. An explicit right inverse is as follows. For an
absolute target vector f, put
\[
 z_i=f_i/(Vm\Gamma),\quad Z=\sum_i z_i,\qquad
 {\cal R}(f)_{ii}=z_i,\quad
 {\cal R}(f)_{ij}=z_i-Z/d\quad(i\ne j).                \tag{3}
\]
Then f(R(f))=f and
\[
 V\operatorname{tr}{\cal R}(f)=\ell\cdot f,\qquad
 \ell_i=1/(m\Gamma)>0.                                \tag{4}
\]

Let g(eta)=DG(0)[eta]. If ell.g is not identically zero, choose a
parameter velocity eta with ell.g(eta)<0 and take
B=-R(g(eta)). Every cap has zero first variation, while volume has
positive first variation. The implicit function theorem applied
using (3) makes all selected cap equalities exact. A sufficiently
smaller right-inverse correction then makes every cap strictly
smaller without losing the positive volume gain. This assertion
requires an open actual compatibility neighborhood.

For the special threshold chart in which cap i depends only on a_i,
sum a_i=1, the stationarity condition is that all numbers
partial G_i/partial a_i be equal. If they are unequal, the choice
eta=-(g-mean(g)1) has the required sign. For affine threshold motions,
the analogous first conditions retain every affine base moment.
For normal motions, they retain the actual global section moments.

## 2. Necessary and sufficient strict quadratic criterion

Assume now
\[
                     \ell\cdot DG(0)=0.              \tag{5}
\]
The full objective-one first stress is then ell. A joint velocity
(B,eta) is critical precisely when
\[
                    f(B)+g(\eta)=0.                 \tag{6}
\]
Its volume first derivative also vanishes, by (4)-(5).

For a critical velocity define the ACTUAL global Lagrangian Hessian
\[
 \begin{split}
 Q(B,\eta)={}&V D^2\det(I)[B,B]\\
 &-\sum_i\ell_i\big(
 D^2_{WW}F_i[B,B]+2D^2_{W\theta}F_i[B,\eta]
                         +D^2_{\theta\theta}G_i[\eta,\eta]\big).
 \end{split}                                                   \tag{7}
\]
All derivatives on the right are at the initial configuration.
The last term is the required baseline correction. Only when the
ENTIRE original-source cap mass is parameter-flat does that term
vanish. The selected-fiber subtraction in (1) removes the pure
theta derivatives of F from the increment, not those of G.

There is a C^2 path with critical first velocity, strictly positive
volume second derivative and strictly negative second derivative of
EVERY cap if and only if Q(B,eta)>0 for some critical velocity.
Here “if and only if” concerns such a STRICT SECOND-ORDER path, not
all possible higher-order escape paths.

Indeed, let q_i be the individual cap second derivatives on the
straight joint path with velocity (B,eta). Add the physical
acceleration
\[
 C={\cal R}(-q-\xi 1),\qquad \xi=\Gamma Q/2.            \tag{8}
\]
Every cap second derivative is then -xi, while volume second
derivative is Q-xi/Gamma=Q/2. Conversely, for any physical and
parameter accelerations, stationarity makes Q equal the volume
second derivative minus ell times the cap second derivatives.
The required strict signs and ell>0 force Q>0.

The exact same reasoning applies at any regularized family whose
original tuple has precisely the prescribed cap budgets. One needs
C^2 convergence and cap-Jacobian surjectivity to pass a strict Q>0
to nearby families; global parameter-flatness is unnecessary.

### Coarea form of the correction

For one cap at one fixed fiber write its margin as
u.x-b, with u nonzero. Along a parameter path let the first and second
margin velocities be w(x) and kappa(x). If the following weighted
section derivative exists with the regularity needed for C^2
differentiation, its contributions to G' and G'' are
\[
 \begin{split}
 G'&=\frac1{|u|}\int_{K\cap\{u.x=b\}}w\,dH_{d-1},\\
 G''&=\frac1{|u|}\int_{K\cap\{u.x=b\}}\kappa\,dH_{d-1}
 -\left.\frac{d}{ds}\right|_{s=0}
   \frac1{|u|}
   \int_{K\cap\{u.x-b=s\}}w(x)^2\,dH_{d-1}.           \tag{9}
 \end{split}
\]
Sum these expressions over the ACTUAL fibers. Formula (9) follows
by fixed-normal Fubini/coarea differentiation of the moving
halfspace boundary; equivalently the second term integrates the
distributional derivative of the halfspace indicator. For a
straight margin path kappa=0. In a normal/meeting-point chart the
margin can have a mixed acceleration; its kappa term must be kept.
The first line retains section centroids; the second retains
derivatives of section second moments. No cap-fraction identity
determines the second line.

## 3. Exact homothetic moment calculation

Take positive compatible fibers r_z K with their common centroid at
zero. An affine centroid section can first be sheared away. Fix a
selected base p and scale the continuous coordinates so r_p=1.
Thus V denotes its volume in these coordinates. Put
\[
 S=\sum_z r_z^{d-1},\qquad N_2=\sum_z r_z^{d-2}.        \tag{10}
\]
For d=2 the summands in N_2 are all 1.

Keep the normals l_i fixed and move the SAME meeting point at every
base:
\[
 H_i(\tau)=\{l_i(x)\ge\tau_i\},\qquad \sum_i\tau_i=0.
\]
This is a whole-space cylindrical cover for every tau. In the common
proper, one-positive-vertex chamber the ORIGINAL entire-source
baseline is
\[
 G_i(\tau)=V\sum_z(r_z h-\tau_i)^d.                   \tag{11}
\]
In particular G_i(0)=Gamma V sum r_z^d, but G_i is not parameter-flat.
Its first and second derivatives along tau=t v are
\[
 G'_i=-Vm\Gamma S v_i,\qquad
 G''_i=V\Gamma\frac{m^2(d-1)}d\,N_2 v_i^2.           \tag{12}
\]
The first stress condition (5) holds because sum v_i=0.

Write b_i=B_ii, r=B1 and let A be the off-diagonal part of B.
Criticality is equivalent to
\[
              \operatorname{tr}B=0,\qquad r=mS v.   \tag{13}
\]
The canonical physical Hessian from
candidate ca3ec9792c38df0f is
\[
 Q_{\rm physical}/V
 =\frac{\|b\|^2}{d}
      -\frac{\|r-b\|^2+\|A\|_F^2}{m}.               \tag{14}
\]
The mixed physical/threshold term, obtained by differentiating the
proper simplex cap formula, contributes
2r.v-2m b.v/d. Combining this with (12) gives
\[
 Q/V=Q_{\rm physical}/V+2r.v-\frac{2m}{d}b.v
                       -\frac{m(d-1)}d N_2\|v\|^2. \tag{15}
\]

For fixed b and r, the unique minimum-norm off-diagonal matrix with
row sums r-b and column sums -b is
\[
 A^{\min}_{ij}
 =\frac{d r_i+r_j-m(b_i+b_j)}{m(d-1)}
 \quad(i\ne j).                                      \tag{16}
\]
Here sum b=sum r=0. Directly summing verifies both marginals.
Its scalar product with any matrix with zero diagonal and zero
row and column sums is zero. Hence A=Amin+Z, where
\[
 \|A\|_F^2=
 \frac{d\|r\|^2-2m r.b+2m\|b\|^2}{m(d-1)}
                         +\|Z\|_F^2.               \tag{17}
\]
This proves the exact completion of squares
\[
 \boxed{\quad
 \frac QV=
 \frac{m(d-1)}d\,\Theta\,\|v\|^2
 -\frac{\|b-b^*\|^2}{d(d-1)}
 -\frac{\|Z\|_F^2}{m},\quad}                         \tag{18}
\]
where
\[
 \Theta=d(S-1)^2+1-N_2,\qquad
 b^*=[d^2S-m(d-1)]v.                                \tag{19}
\]
Thus Theta>0 is NECESSARY AND SUFFICIENT for a strict quadratic
escape in this specified one-fiber, fixed-normal, common-meeting-
translation parameter space. In particular (18) includes all
physical simplex velocities, not merely a selected test direction.

An explicit maximizing physical matrix is
\[
 \begin{split}
 B_{ii}&=[d^2S-m(d-1)]v_i,\\
 B_{ij}&=(m-dS)v_i+m(1-S)v_j\quad(i\ne j).             \tag{20}
 \end{split}
\]
Its column sums and trace are zero and its row sums are mS v.

## 4. Identical fibers, smallest fibers, and a sharp limitation

For N >= 2 identical fibers, S=N_2=N, and
\[
                  \Theta=(N-1)[d(N-1)-1]>0.         \tag{21}
\]
For THREE identical fibers, (20) becomes
B_ii=(2d^2+1)v_i and
B_ij=-(2d-1)v_i-2m v_j. Its exact Hessian is
\[
 Q=V\frac{m(d-1)(4d-2)}d\|v\|^2>0.                 \tag{22}
\]
For d=2 and v=(1,-1,0), Q/V=18. This is an asymmetric actual source:
take the three integer fibers K,K,K at -1,0,1. The simplex is not
centrally symmetric, and its baseline (11) has nonzero curvature.

More generally, if p has a SMALLEST radius, every other normalized
radius is at least one. Consequently
\[
 \sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-2}
 \le \sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{2d-2}
 \le \left(\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-1}\right)^2,
\]
so Theta>0 whenever another positive fiber exists.

The assertion is false for an ARBITRARILY selected fiber in this
fixed-normal/common-translation class. For two actual fibers K and
tK at bases 0 and 1, selecting K gives
\[
                     \Theta=t^{d-2}(dt^d-1).        \tag{23}
\]
For 0<t^d<1/d this is strictly negative. These are the exact fibers
of their convex hull; the support {0,1} is lattice-complete and
compatibility is open. Every canonical cap fraction is Gamma in
both fibers. By (18) the critical Hessian is negative definite.
The cap derivative has full rank and all multipliers are positive;
the usual local coordinate proof of the constrained second-order
sufficient condition therefore makes this a strict local maximum
for this one-free-fiber, fixed-normal, common-translation problem.
Equivalently, eliminate the cap-equality coordinates using (3);
the remaining objective has negative-definite Hessian, and cap
decreases have negative objective coefficient ell>0.

This is an actual-source obstruction to ignoring the baseline
curvature or claiming a positive common-translation Hessian for
every selected fiber. It does NOT rule out independent normal
rotations, different affine threshold motions, higher-order
behavior when Theta=0, or movement of other fibers. The general
criterion (7) is the appropriate test for those enlarged charts.

Without scaling, the positive-sign condition is
\[
 d\left(\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-1}\right)^2
       >r_p^d\sum_{z\ne p}r_z^{d-2}.                \tag{24}
\]

## 5. Removing active compatibility using the flat radial barrier

Assume P=conv(P) intersect Z^n, P is finite and spans R^n, every
fiber is positive, and the original homothetic simplex family is
compatible. Let |P|>=2. Its affine centroid section is interior.

Apply radial-layer-barrier-flat-strictification.md. It gives
arbitrarily close positive radial homothets, normalized to exactly
the original total mixed mass M, with a UNIFORM positive support
gap for every excluded-self barycentric representation. Every
canonical cap still has exactly Gamma M, because its fraction is
Gamma in each fiber. The gap gives an open neighborhood of
independent physical fiber perturbations whose convex hull has
EXACTLY the prescribed fibers on P and no additional integer bases.

Select a smallest-radius fiber of the original family. By (19)
its strict positive Hessian persists after a sufficiently small
radial strictification. All functions here are analytic in the
positive radii, the physical vertex matrix, and the proper
thresholds: (11) and the labeled simplex cap formula supply this
directly. No smoothing or unsupported C^2 assertion is needed.

At that strictified family take (20) and any nonzero sum-zero v.
Use the acceleration (8), now with its current selected volume and
cap derivatives. The resulting path has total mass
M+(Q/4)t^2+o(t^2), while every selected cap has mass
Gamma M-(Gamma Q/4)t^2+o(t^2). Choosing t sufficiently small preserves
the uniform compatibility gap, all proper cuts, and the exact
whole-space group cover. Therefore the actual mass increases and
ALL selected budgets strictly decrease.

Only the selected fiber changes after the preliminary radial
stage; the other fibers' genuine threshold curvature is exactly
the N_2 term in (18). This proves the stated extension beyond both
central symmetry and parameter-flat cap families.

The finite-base relative-lattice reduction can be used if P has
deficient affine rank, preserving its saturated base lattice and
all d-volume fibers. The primary statement above uses full rank
to avoid claiming an unmentioned full-ambient completion.
Zero-volume fibers may instead be removed by taking the hull of
the positive support when that reduction is desired; no Hausdorff
approximation to removed base-only pieces is asserted here.

These sources already have the usual affine-centroid selector
guarantee from weighted Doignon and ordinary Grünbaum. The result
is a physical selected-cover variation theorem, not a new OC case
and not a classification of arbitrary active cap covers.

## 6. Equal canonical fractions force the homothetic class

The shape hypothesis in Section 5 follows automatically from the
following equal-fraction data. Let the initial group consist of the
m canonical centroid caps of ONE selected simplex, through the same
affine interior section q(z). Suppose its fraction in EVERY positive
fiber is the same as in that selected simplex, for each cap. Each
fraction is therefore exactly Gamma.

We prove, without an assumed multiple-cap equality classification,
that every fiber must be q(z)+r_z K, with r_z>0.

Fix a fiber B and shear its meeting point to zero. Write its centroid
as g. If l_i(g)>0, moving the cap l_i>=0 parallel to the through-g
position removes strictly positive volume: an intervening open slab
meets an interior neighborhood of g. Ordinary Grünbaum says the
through-g cap already has volume at least Gamma |B|. This contradicts
the original cap's volume Gamma |B|. Therefore l_i(g)<=0 for every i.
Since sum l_i=0 and the normals span R^d, all these values vanish and
g=0. This step uses the known full canonical circuit directly; it
needs no additional exterior-contact theorem.

For every y in B, some selected cap contains y because the group
covers R^d. That cap has mass Gamma |B|. Thus the ordinary maximum
normalized depth D(B) is at most Gamma, and ordinary Grünbaum gives
the opposite bound at g. The already proved and independently
audited theorem in
candidate e2c55c91458e1e8c now gives that
B is a simplex.

It remains to identify its orientation, which does not follow just
from knowing it is some simplex. The ordinary single-cap equality
case is stated precisely, with its primary source, in Section 1 of
that same note: a centroid equality cap is the apex-side cut of a
pyramid with base parallel to the cut. Applied to a simplex B, its
apex is an extreme point, hence one of B's vertices; all remaining
vertices lie in its base, so that base is exactly the opposite
facet. Thus each selected l_i is a positive multiple of one of B's
opposite-facet barycentric gradients.

The m canonical directions of K are distinct, and B has exactly m
facets. Relabel B's barycentrics mu_i to match them. There are
positive constants c_i with
\[
                  \nabla\mu_i=c_i l_i.
\]
Here l_i denotes the linear functional, or its gradient vector, as
appropriate. Both sum grad mu_i=0 and sum l_i=0. The fixed canonical
normal matrix has rank d, so its dependence space is one-dimensional;
hence every c_i equals a common c>0. Because g=0 is B's centroid,
mu_i(0)=1/m, and therefore
\[
 \mu_i(x)=1/m+c\,l_i(x),\qquad
 B=\{x:l_i(x)\ge-1/(mc)\}=(1/c)K.                    \tag{25}
\]
Restoring q(z) gives the claimed homothetic family with affine
centroid section. The cap orientation is essential in taking c>0.

Consequently Sections 1--5 establish this broader conclusion:

**One canonical equal-fraction group.** For d>=2 and a finite
lattice-complete full-rank positive support with at least two
fibers, suppose an affine interior section and a selected simplex
supply one whole-space canonical group having the same cap
fractions in every fiber. Then those fractions are Gamma, all
fibers are aligned homothetic simplices about that section, and an
arbitrarily close exact cap-flat radial strictification followed
by motion of one smallest-radius fiber and the common meeting
point increases total mass and strictly decreases every selected
cap budget.

This does not claim escape for a prescribed larger fiber, preserve
unselected cap budgets, or replace the exact canonical equal-fraction
hypothesis by arbitrary matching fractions from a noncanonical
simplex cut tuple.
